questions.question_text: Which expression represents **"$5$ is added to $x$, then the result is doubled"**?

options.why: Doubled only $x$; 'the result' is the whole sum $x + 5$, which needs brackets.
Doubled the $5$ only and left $x$ unchanged.
Added $2$ instead of doubling; 'doubled' means multiply by $2$.
Describes $2(n + 3)$; here the doubling applies to $n$ only, not to $n + 3$.
Uses subtraction; the $+3$ means add $3$, not subtract it.
Swapped the coefficient and constant; here $2$ is the multiplier and $3$ is added.

questions.solution_text:
$2n = \text{double } n$
$2n + 3 = 3 \text{ more than that}$
$3$ more than double $n$

questions.question_text: Which expression represents **"$w$ is subtracted from $20$, then the result is multiplied by $5$"**?

options.why: Reversed the subtraction; 'subtracted from $20$' means $20 - w$, not $w - 20$.
Multiplied only $w$ by $5$; the whole result $(20 - w)$ is what gets multiplied.
Multiplied the $20$ by $5$ first instead of subtracting before multiplying.

questions.question_text:
Mary has $k$ trading cards.
Luke has 7 fewer trading cards than Mary.
Which expression represents Luke's trading cards?

options.why: Divides by 7 instead of subtracting seven cards from Mary's number.
Adds seven, which represents seven more cards rather than seven fewer.

questions.solution_text: Starting with Mary's $k$ cards, taking away 7 gives Luke $k-7$ cards.

questions.question_text:
There are $c$ crisps in a packet of crisps.
You buy 2 packets and then eat 10 crisps.
How many crisps do you have left?

options.why: This reverses the roles of packets and crisps.
This subtracts before accounting for two packets.
This adds one packet instead of doubling c.

questions.solution_text: Two packets contain $2c$ crisps. After eating 10, the number left is $2c-10$.
